article-wildlife-heroes-supports-the-aus.description: We are proud to have sponsored the Australian Wildlife Rehabilitation Conference and funded Wildlife Heroes scholarships for 10 NSW wildlife carers.

article-wildlife-heroes-upcoming-activit.description: Our Wildlife Heroes plan for the year ahead includes a grant round for medium to large assets and emergency preparedness training for NSW rehabilitators.

article-wildlife-heroes-updates-from-the.description: Wildlife Heroes Project Manager Stacey Mole has been on the road meeting NSW volunteer wildlife rescue groups to shape the project's next plan.

article-wildlife-heroes-wildlife-rescue-.title: Wildlife Heroes Wildlife Rescue Handbook
article-wildlife-heroes-wildlife-rescue-.description: Knowing what to do as first on the scene can save an animal's life. Our new Wildlife Heroes Wildlife Rescue Handbook covers the first 24 hours.

article-wildlife-heroes.html.description: Our NSW Wildlife Heroes Project is offering grants of up to $15,000 per group for medium to large assets that help volunteers rehabilitate wildlife.

article-wollombi-and-laguna-primary-scho.description: Wollombi Landcare and 20 students from Laguna Public School planted around 90 trees from Hawkesbury Community Nursery on Earth Day 2021 with our support.

article-wombatrescues.html.description: Flooded burrows left wombats sheltering under houses. Our Wildlife Heroes NSW Flood Emergency Grant helped LAOKO give displaced wombats a dry bed.

article-years-of-restoration-written-in-.description: A morning in Hindmarsh Valley National Park, where a cleared paddock is becoming forest again, and why connection matters more than tree counts.

article-your-backyard-is-habitat-too-hel.description: Most of the green on a city map is mown lawn native animals cannot use. A backyard, courtyard or balcony planted with local natives becomes a safe step.

bequests-professional-advisers.html.title: Gifts in Wills for Professional Advisers
bequests-professional-advisers.html.description: For solicitors, estate planners, financial advisers and executors: our legal name, ABN and suggested wording for gifts in wills, plus one person to call.

bequests.html.title: Gifts in Wills
bequests.html.description: Leave a gift in your will and keep the nature you love living on. See how one gift helped save Mundoo Island, and how to leave a gift of your own.

corporate-governance.html.description: We are accountable to our supporters, our partners and the ACNC. Our board, constitution, policies and financial reporting, and how we are run.

donate-land.html.description: Give land with conservation value to become national park, protected by law for good. We assess the land, secure agreement and manage the transfer.

faqs.html.description: Answers to common questions about who we are, donating, tax receipts, monthly giving, gifts in wills, volunteering, grants and how to reach us.

government-partnerships.html.description: Trusted by government since 1970 to deliver conservation at landscape scale. We bring Traditional Owners, funding and delivery partners to one table.

grants.html.description: Our conservation grants have supported projects that protect native habitats, wildlife and cultural heritage. Programs are closed; see what they funded.

growing-national-parks.html.description: We expand and protect conservation spaces to safeguard critical habitats. Our land acquisitions and park expansions, from the Flinders Ranges to the coast.

healing-the-land.html.description: We restore landscapes affected by bushfires, floods and land clearing through our Landscape Resilience Program: revegetation, wetlands and cultural fire.

how-your-contributions-help.html.description: Every donation is put to work across our three pillars, funding conservation projects Australia-wide with First Nations groups, rangers and scientists.

in-the-news.html.description: Where we have been covered in the press, on radio and on television, from koala food trees in Lismore to our Wildlife Friendly Vets program.

index.html.title: Foundation for National Parks & Wildlife | Since 1970

media-enquiry.html.description: Talking wildlife, national parks or one of our projects? We can help with interviews, imagery and background. Email fnpw@fnpw.org.au or call 1800 898 626.

newsletter-thank-you.html.description: Thank you for signing up. You are now part of a community helping us protect and restore Australia's national parks and wildlife. Stories are on their way.

newsletters-sign-up.html.description: Sign up to our monthly email newsletter for project updates, species spotlights, stories about the difference your support makes and new ways to help.

partner-invest.html.description: Partner with us to deliver conservation at scale. We find the priorities that matter most, bring partners and funding together and stay to show results.

partner.html.description: We work with businesses ready to commit serious capital to conservation of national significance, from land for new national parks to restoring regions.

paws-magazine.html.description: Read past issues of PAWS Magazine, with updates from the conservation projects our partners and supporters fund. Our newsletters are now digital only.

privacy-policy.html.description: How we collect, hold, use and disclose personal information, and how you can access or correct it or make a complaint. Effective November 2026.

project-1-million-turtles.html.description: Citizen science at a scale that can actually move a population, aimed at the freshwater turtles of the Murray-Darling, down 91 per cent.

project-bushfire-recovery-seedbanks.html.description: Seeds are the cornerstone of any revegetation project. Our Seedbanks build community capacity to identify endemic species and secure their seed after fire.

project-cultivating-koala-habitat.html.description: With Wollondilly Shire Council we restored four hectares of koala habitat corridor along the Bargo River: 2,000 local plants, 95 per cent still alive.

project-curb-wombat-mange-program.html.description: A two million dollar rapid response fund, put into the hands of the people already treating bare-nosed wombats for sarcoptic mange across their range.

project-enhancing-biodiversity-protectin.title: Biodiversity and Cultural Heritage at Torrens Island
project-enhancing-biodiversity-protectin.description: On Torrens Island near Adelaide, Kaurna youth overseen by Elders are trialling Cocoon plant incubators to revegetate woodland on a cultural site.

project-fire-wise.html.description: Native planting, used deliberately, so that preparing for fire and protecting habitat stop being opposite things. Our Fire Wise project in VIC, SA and NSW.

project-garners-beach-cassowary-rehabili.title: Garner's Beach Cassowary Rehabilitation Centre
project-garners-beach-cassowary-rehabili.description: The Garner's Beach Cassowary Rehabilitation Centre has cared for sick, injured and orphaned Southern Cassowaries, an endangered species, since 2001.

project-genetic-code-of-koalas.html.description: We funded the Australian Museum to read the DNA of koalas around Port Macquarie and find out whether they were still reaching each other.

project-kaurna-cultural-fire-field-river.description: Kaurna-led cultural fire at Kauwi-marnirla (Field River) in Adelaide's south, backed by $4.07 million from the Disaster Ready Fund, led by Kaurna Kardla.

project-mundoo-island-acquisition.html.description: 1,900 hectares at the Murray Mouth, farmed for more than a century, secured in 2025 and now being added to Coorong National Park for 65 threatened species.

project-native-plant-nurseries.html.description: Only a tenth of Australia's native plants are available as seed, so we built a network of more than thirty community-led nurseries to grow the rest.

project-nectar-sippers.html.description: Three woodland birds that follow the flowering, a farming landscape they can no longer cross, and four years spent giving them somewhere to land.

project-nilpena-nationalpark.html.description: Sixty thousand hectares of the Flinders Ranges holding the world's richest record of early complex life. We helped fund the acquisition of Nilpena Station.

project-supporting-community-led-treatme.title: Community-led treatment to protect bare-nosed wombats
project-supporting-community-led-treatme.description: Through the Curb Wombat Mange Program we helped expand community-led treatment of sarcoptic mange in bare-nosed wombats across New South Wales.

project-tangaroa-blue.html.description: Eleven million data points from beach clean-ups, turned into plans that stop the rubbish arriving. We backed Tangaroa Blue's source reduction work in 2018.

saving-species.html.description: We protect Australia's most vulnerable species by restoring habitat, creating wildlife corridors and supporting recovery programs across the country.

search.html.description: Search our projects, stories, reports and ways to get involved, from growing national parks to saving species and healing the land.

terms-and-conditions.html.description: The terms and conditions that govern use of our website and its contents, published by the Foundation for National Parks & Wildlife, ABN 90 107 744 771.

thank-you-volunteer-form.html.description: Thank you for your interest in our corporate volunteering day. Your request has been submitted and we will be in touch shortly with next steps.

thank-you.html.description: Thank you for your support. Your gift grows national parks, saves species and heals the land, and you are officially one of the good ones.

ways-you-can-get-involved.html.description: Donate, volunteer, partner, fundraise or leave a gift in your will. Four ways to give and four ways to give time and influence, however you want to help.

why-your-support-is-needed.html.description: Australia is home to species found nowhere else, and one of the worst extinction records on Earth. Your support is not optional; it is the whole mechanism.

workplace-giving.html.description: A small amount from each pay, before tax, often matched by your employer. Set and forget, and it adds up to habitat for our native wildlife.

about.html.title: About FNPW: 55 years of Australian conservation

article-turtle-talk.html.description: Since 2018 we have worked closely with Ricky Spencer from Western Sydney University to coordinate school engagement in the 1 Million Turtle Project.
